direct_answer: Gabapentin and pregabalin are sometimes prescribed for nerve pain. Common side effects include dizziness and drowsiness, which can raise falls risk in frail older people. Do not stop them suddenly. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review if you feel unsteady.

content:
These medicines can help some types of nerve pain, but side effects matter more with frailty.

This guide explains the risks and what to ask. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

What they are used for

They are used for nerve pain and some other conditions. They are not usually used for osteoarthritis joint pain alone.

Side effects

  • Dizziness.
  • Drowsiness.
  • Unsteadiness.
  • Confusion in some older people.

Reducing risk

  • Do not stop suddenly.
  • Avoid alcohol.
  • Take care when standing up.
  • Ask for a medicine review.

Questions to ask

  • Is this still helping?
  • Could the dose be reduced?
  • Are there alternatives?

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I stop if I feel dizzy?

Talk to your GP first; stopping suddenly can cause problems.

Are they addictive?

They can cause dependence, so they are reviewed carefully.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Gabapentin
  • NHS: Pregabalin
